title: Fail-closed source and publication evidence admission
instruction: Write solution.py defining solve(value). The input is a JSON object of synthetic evidence claims. Return exactly an object with keys admitted (a boolean) and reason (a string). Apply the following checks in the listed order, stopping at the first failure: (1) source_sha must be a string of exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters; otherwise return admitted=false, reason='invalid_source'. (2) runtime_source_sha must meet the same format; otherwise reason='invalid_runtime_source'. (3) Those two strings must be equal; otherwise reason='source_mismatch'. (4) artifact_verified must be the JSON boolean true, not the number 1 or a nonempty string; otherwise reason='artifact_unverified'. (5) publication_status must equal the exact string 'success'; skipped, failure, missing, or any other value fails with reason='publication_not_success'. (6) runtime_healthy must be the JSON boolean true; otherwise reason='runtime_not_healthy'. If all checks pass return admitted=true, reason='admitted'. Missing fields fail their respective check; ignore extra fields. Do not change the input. Here runtime_source_sha means the runtime's declared SOURCE revision, NOT its provider repository revision. This pure function only classifies supplied claims; it does not authenticate evidence, contact a provider, or establish real production readiness. Use only Python's standard library.
